$comment: The release-parity ledger. It records which runners are actually compared against each other, and — just as importantly — which are NOT, so three green ticks in CI are never mistaken for a three-way comparison. scripts/cross-check.mjs reads cross_checked and FAILS when a runner declared here is missing on disk: a runner it quietly skipped would let the remaining ones agree with each other and call that parity.

cross_checked.setup: composer install in runners/php. Installs the published particle-academy/prism, not a working copy — the reference the corpus is generated from has to be a released artefact, or the goldens describe someone's uncommitted branch.
Checkout Particle-Academy/prism-ts beside this repository, npm ci, npm run build, and npm install this repo's loaders/ts.
Checkout Particle-Academy/prism-py beside this repository, pip install -e ., and pip install this repo's loaders/py.

$not_cross_checked_comment: Recorded rather than omitted. An implementation asserted only by its own suite is a weaker claim than one compared against a sibling, and the difference should be visible.
$gaps_comment: Places where a green tick means less than it looks. Each is also recorded on the suite manifest it affects; this is the index.

gaps.summary: The reference has no error codes, so the PHP runner reaches its verdict on the text-errors suite by MATCHING ON PROSE — in a suite whose argument is that prose is not the contract.

SERIALISE half CLOSED: the reference no longer renders a map-typed field as an empty JSON array, so trs-0006 and rtp-0009 are enforced in all three languages rather than skipped in two. DECODE half OPEN and unclosable: json_decode('{}', true) and json_decode('[]', true) are the same value, so no PHP-authored case INPUT can carry the distinction either — which is why jci-0001 states it as raw strings and skips php, and why rtp-0009 discriminates on ts and py only.
gaps.closed_note: Closing it needed two mechanisms, not one. A key-aware wrap (Prism\Prism\Support\JsonMap) for fields Prism DECLARES to be maps and defaults to empty — there is no input to carry, so the declaration is the only evidence. And a container-preserving decode (Prism\Prism\Support\Json::decode(..., preservingContainerTypes: true)) for arbitrary JSON, where the distinction is CARRIED from the input rather than guessed at the output: a {} nested three levels inside a tool call's arguments is reached by no key-aware rule. Promoting every empty array instead would render "required": [] as {} and trade one silent divergence for a commoner one.

gaps.summary: The reference can serialise its value objects and cannot read them back, so the rehydration half of every roundtrip row is unverified in PHP.
JavaScript rounds integers above 2^53 and cannot detect that it has, so the TypeScript port cannot answer the large-integer identity row.

procedure: 1. Regenerate goldens against the RELEASED reference: composer update in runners/php, then php tools/generate-goldens.php. A golden generated against a working copy describes someone's uncommitted branch.
2. node tools/sync-corpus.mjs — the loader packages each ship their own copy of the fixtures.
3. node tools/guard-corpus.mjs — corpus invariants, including the unquoted-large-integer scan.
4. node tools/parity-check.mjs --report — the existence check and the drift report. A missing mirror fails here; a conformance suite could never have caught it.
5. Run every loader's own tests. All of them are required CI jobs; a loader whose tests run nowhere is a claim about coverage rather than coverage.
6. node scripts/cross-check.mjs — every runner, identical verdicts.

7. Bump VERSION when the corpus content changed at all, not only when a case was added. Ports pin the corpus EXACTLY and assert the version is current; a caret on a 0.x locks the minor and silently strands a port on a stale contract.
8. Update kit_version and the kit block in manifest/packages.json, and corpus_version here.
